**What type of PR is this?**


/kind feature


**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This changes the `pod_preemption_victims` from Gauge to Histogram. More discussion about this is mentioned in the #83464.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--

-->
Fixes #83464

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Change `pod_preemption_victims` metric from Gauge to Histogram.
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

This section can be blank if this pull request does not require a release note.

See here for guidance on getting permanent links to files: https://help.github.com/en/articles/getting-permanent-links-to-files

Please use the following format for linking documentation:
- [KEP]: <link>
- [Usage]: <link>
- [Other doc]: <link>
-->
```docs

```

review_comments:
BTW: do we break the original metrics by changing this to the histogram? This is in the alpha stage, so it implies we don't guarantee the compatibility of the metrics, right? 

But I think we do need a release note for this.
@draveness Thanks for the review. I have included a release note and squashed the commits.

> BTW: do we break the original metrics by changing this to the histogram? This is in the alpha stage, so it implies we don't guarantee the compatibility of the metrics, right?

That's my understanding as well. @piosz, can you give us some feedback on this?

According to [stability-classes](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/20190404-kubernetes-control-plane-metrics-stability.md#stability-classes),
`Alpha metrics have no stability guarantees; as such they can be modified or deleted at any time. `.

I agree with @draveness release note is necessary and it's enough, even though a little rough.
